title: Add tvOS platform port
body:
> **Status:** this PR was closed in favor of the human-driven #118332. The work
> continues on the `tvos-port` branch of
> [sanarena/godot](https://github.com/sanarena/godot/tree/tvos-port), which is
> what ships real games to Apple TV today — the description below tracks that
> branch, and any of the code is free to take as reference for #118332.
> The branch README
> ([platform/tvos/README.md](https://github.com/sanarena/godot/blob/tvos-port/platform/tvos/README.md))
> carries the same supported / verified split.

This adds tvOS as an export platform, built on the shared apple_embedded stack
next to iOS and visionOS. It covers building the engine for tvOS (device and
simulator), exporting through a new tvOS preset, playing with the Siri Remote
and game controllers, and typing through the native tvOS keyboard.

Related proposal: godotengine/godot-proposals#13532

Developed against a real 2D game with the Compatibility renderer, run on Apple
TV hardware (A10X) and in the tvOS Simulator. 3D games are not tested, and the
Metal renderer has not drawn a real game yet (no Apple4+ TV available). Full
details below.

## What works and how it was tested

Build and export

- `scons platform=tvos` builds device templates and
  `scons platform=tvos simulator=yes` builds simulator templates. Both package
  into tvos.zip through the normal template flow.
- The editor gets a tvOS export preset (device types, bundle id, signing,
  icons, launch storyboard). Export, sign and install were verified end to
  end: the game installs on Apple TV hardware and launches from the home
  screen.
- New CI workflow `.github/workflows/tvos_builds.yml` builds template_release
  for device and simulator, hooked into runner.yml.

Running a 2D game on Apple TV hardware (Apple TV 4K 1st gen, A10X, tvOS 26.6)

- A complete 2D game (menus, settings panels, popups, gameplay, networked
  rooms) runs and plays normally with the Compatibility renderer, all the way
  from login through rounds to result panels.
- Siri Remote arrives as **key events** on device and simulator alike: swipes
  are the arrow keys, click is Enter, Play/Pause is MEDIAPLAY. A 6-button
  matrix on hardware confirmed every button with press+release and the exact
  keycodes, with zero joystick events (the remote is not a joystick, so
  nothing doubles; MFi pads still use the joypad API).
- Menu goes back (`WINDOW_EVENT_GO_BACK_REQUEST`, log-verified on hardware)
  when `quit_on_go_back` is off, and hands the press back to UIKit (system
  Menu-to-Home flow) when it is on. The app stays in the foreground in both
  modes.
- `SceneTree.quit()` is a warned no-op on tvOS: the main loop keeps running
  (frame counter advances on hardware) and the system suspends the app.
- `user://` maps to `Library/Caches`: the tvOS sandbox denies file creation
  in Documents, so a Documents-backed `user://` breaks on first write on
  device (proven with a native probe; Caches writes round-trip).
- Text entry: the native tvOS keyboard opens from game text fields, and
  typing, deleting, Done/confirm and Menu dismiss all write the correct text
  back into the field. Verified in more than one field, including a max
  length limited one and editing prefilled text.
- Metal (Forward+/Mobile): the tvOS GPU/MSL profiles and `appletvos` shader
  toolchain are implemented; on the A10X box both renderers show the
  capability alert naming the detected family ("this GPU reports Apple3").
  The toolchain query itself (`xcrun -sdk appletvos metal -mtargetos=...`)
  is verified on the Mac.

Simulator

- The same game runs in the tvOS Simulator with OpenGL ES, including a full
  practice round (settings toggle, bomb, blast breaking bricks, player
  damage) driven by injected remote presses.
- FP/Mobile simulator builds fail gracefully at the capability gate (the sim
  GPU reports Apple1/Apple2, tier-1 argument buffers, no image cube arrays —
  characterized with a native probe), so Metal stays enabled and links.
- Automated XCUITest suites pass on the simulator: nickname entry end to end,
  room code entry with max length enforcement, and editing prefilled text
  (testNicknameEndToEnd, testRoomCodeKeyboard, testPrefilledCaretZeroRepro).
- Headless suite `tests/tvos_remote_regression.gd` (in the game repo):
  101 checks on the input map, remote buttons, pause/back routing, menu
  navigation, walking, bubbles and suspend/resume — all green.

Not tested

- 3D games. Only 2D was run, so please treat every 3D path as unverified.
- Forward+/Mobile pixels with a real game: needs an Apple4+ Apple TV, which
  was not available. Profiles, toolchain, linking and gating are verified;
  rendering is not.
- Physical MFi controllers (no hardware), the `pressesCancelled` stuck-key
  path (no deterministic trigger), App Store submission, and tvOS versions
  outside the tested 26.x device / 26.5–27 simulators.

## How it is put together

Platform and build

- platform/tvos: detect.py, SCsub, OS_TVOS, DisplayServerTVOS, main loop and
  app delegate glue, tvOS display layers (GDTMetalLayer/GDTOpenGLLayer), the
  export plugin, EditorExportPlatformTVOS docs, README.
- methods.py and platform_methods.py learn the appletvos/appletvsimulator SDKs
  and Swift targets. drivers/SCsub and drivers/sdl/SCsub include tvOS in the
  Apple and SDL driver lists.
- tvOS specifics in the shared code: no touchscreen, clipboard or orientation
  features; OS.execute/OS.create_process fail with ERR_UNAVAILABLE since the
  sandbox forbids spawning; iconv loads the same dylib as iOS/macOS;
  TVOS_SIMULATOR counts for OS.has_feature("simulator"); the Apple emoji
  baseline fix covers tvOS; the editor spells the platform "tvOS".

Input

- GDTViewController subclasses GCEventViewController on tvOS. Siri Remote
  presses are synthesized to keys in `pressesBegan`/`pressesEnded` on device
  AND simulator (arrows, Enter, MEDIAPLAY for Play/Pause); MFi pads take the
  same SDL MFI gamepad path as on iOS. SDL remote-as-joystick stays off so a
  press is never reported twice.
- Menu is special: with `quit_on_go_back` the began+ended pair goes back to
  UIKit (with `controllerUserInteractionEnabled = NO` so Menu is not eaten as
  controller input); without it, release sends
  `WINDOW_EVENT_GO_BACK_REQUEST`. Same idea as the Android back button.
  `pressesCancelled` releases any keys the system stole mid-press.
- New DisplayServer::is_keyboard_active() (default false, implemented by the
  Apple embedded server). JoypadSDL drains joystick events while the native
  keyboard is up so typing on the remote does not also drive the game behind
  it. Button releases always pass so nothing sticks down.

Text entry

- tvOS can not use the iOS input view: UITextView editing is unavailable there
  and UIKeyInput on a custom view never brings the keyboard up. So there is a
  new GDTKeyboardInputField, a hidden UITextField driven through the existing
  virtual_keyboard_show/hide path.
- tvOS owns the keyboard cursor (append only, no caret reporting), so on every
  change the field mirrors its whole text into Godot: caret to end, clear,
  retype. Keystroke diffing against a recorded caret was tried first and
  merged old and new text, which is why it works this way.
- The field enforces the Godot max length, a Menu dismiss sends Escape
  (ui_cancel) so the LineEdit stops editing, and hiding from Godot's side
  does not send a stray Escape.

Rendering

- GLES3 takes the same guards as iOS: no program binary cache, no S3TC
  assumption, no multiview paths, no OVR multiview calls. Oversize textures
  are downscaled instead of rendering black.
- Metal tvOS device profiles (Apple1-9 x tvOS 15-26 MSL ladder),
  `TARGET_OS_TV` platform mapping, and the `appletvos` SDK/mtargetos shader
  toolchain. Simulator-only link and heap shims keep sim Metal templates
  building; they fail at the capability gate, never misrender.
- The Apple4 capability gate names the detected family in the alert instead
  of failing with an empty list.
- The Metal 64 byte uniform buffer offset alignment now applies to
  TARGET_OS_TV too.
- Content scale comes from the window scene once the view is in the window
  (UIScreen.mainScreen is deprecated on tvOS 26). The OpenGL renderbuffer
  derives its size from the layer scale, so a stale scale rendered at the
  wrong resolution.
- If a project requests opengl3 from a Metal only build, the display server
  warns and falls back to Metal instead of failing later.

Quit and storage

- `SceneTree.quit()` returns early with a warning on Apple embedded
  platforms (documented in SceneTree.xml): termination is forbidden there,
  tvOS leaves through the Menu flow.
- `OS_AppleEmbedded::get_user_data_dir()` points tvOS at `Library/Caches`
  (Documents is unwritable in the tvOS sandbox).

SDL

- SDL platform name "tvOS".
- dlmalloc is forced to mmap only, since tvOS forbids sbrk (same effect as its
  DARWIN branch).
- Godot's SDL snapshot has no sys filesystem driver for Apple platforms, but
  SDL_IOFromFile (used for gamepad mapping files) calls SDL_GetPrefPath there.
  So drivers/sdl now ships a small SDL_GetPrefPath rooted at the app Documents
  folder. It compiles for all three Apple embedded platforms.

Export details

- tvos.zip registered in the export template manager under Mobile.
- Parallax `.imagestack` app icons (no scale key; actool infers it from the
  layer dimensions) and Top Shelf images with Xcode's role strings.
- The shared iOS launch storyboard is retargeted at export time to the AppleTV
  storyboard shape (targetRuntime, no device/deployment tags), and the launch
  image file name substitution the shared template expects is filled in.
- The generated Info.plist drops iOS-only keys (CFBundleIcons, LSRequiresIPhoneOS,
  UIRequiresFullScreen, UIStatusBarHidden, camera/mic/photo descriptions, iPad
  orientations) and visionOS-only usage descriptions; camera/mic/photos/Files
  export options are hidden.
- visionOS only plist keys are blanked. Tinted icon options and the iPhone/iPad
  only device capability options are hidden behind
  _supports_tinted_icons()/_supports_device_capability_options() virtuals that
  tvOS overrides.
- libgodot.tvos.debug/release.xcframework skeletons mirroring the
  iOS/visionOS ones.

## Notes

- Every shared file change is behind TVOS_ENABLED / APPLE_EMBEDDED or a
  virtual, so iOS/visionOS behavior should be untouched; the iOS release
  template builds cleanly on this branch.
- As said above: 3D is untested and the Metal renderer has not drawn a real
  game yet (needs Apple4+ hardware).
- Since this PR is closed, review discussion for the ongoing work happens on
  the `tvos-port` branch; happy to split it into smaller PRs (platform,
  input/keyboard, export, CI) against #118332's direction if that helps.

## Ready-to-use package (no compiling)

New to this? Grab the prebuilt editor + export template + setup guide
from the GitHub release (Apple Silicon macOS):

**https://github.com/sanarena/godot/releases/tag/appletv-4.8.dev-3e88277fe6**

Contents: `Godot_tvOS.app.zip` (editor, 4.8.dev @ tvos-port 3e88277fe6),
`tvos.tpz` (export template), `GUIDE.md` (5-minute setup: simulator and
real Apple TV), `version.txt`, `SHA256SUMS.txt`. The shipped editor was
verified end to end: it exported BubblyField, built for the tvOS
simulator, and ran (screenshot-tested).
